articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures stunning images of stellar jets emerging from a nebula. Webb's observations reveal the dynamic and violent processes of star birth.

articles.title: Webb Captures This Golden Galaxy Cluster in All it's Glory
articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features the brilliant golden galaxies belonging to the MACS J0454.1-0300 galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a magnificent golden galaxy cluster in stunning detail. This image showcases the universe's breathtaking beauty and complexity.

articles.title: Cosmic 'hamburger' offers rare edge-on view of where giant planets may take shape
articles.description: Astronomers using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) were surprised to discover the earliest phases of giant planet formation between the dense layers of gas and dust in the "Gomez's Hamburger" system, referred to as GoHam.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Using ALMA, astronomers discovered a rare edge-on cosmic structure revealing the earliest phases of giant planet formation in an unprecedented direct view of planetary genesis.

articles.title: Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars
articles.description: Japanese scientists will launch a spacecraft on Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars' moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Japan will launch a historic spacecraft mission to retrieve samples from one of Mars' moons, achieving a world-first accomplishment in planetary exploration.

articles.title: Two monster black holes could collide in just 100 years
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, with observations suggesting the pair completes an orbit every 121 days. Depending on their masses, these cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.
articles.summary: Astronomers found compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward collision within approximately 100 years, a landmark discovery in understanding black hole dynamics.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a strange universal rule behind black hole eruptions
articles.description: Scientists have discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes appear to launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. The breakthrough could explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will happen.
articles.summary: Astronomers discover a universal rule governing how black holes of different sizes launch powerful jets. This breakthrough reveals fundamental physics principles applicable across vastly different scales.

articles.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
articles.description: Japan just launched an epic mission to Mars' moons that could make history as the first spacecraft to return to Earth from the Red Planet — and it plans to come back with samples onboard.
articles.summary: Japan launches the groundbreaking MMX mission to return samples from Mars' moon Phobos to Earth. This historic endeavor marks the first attempt to bring Martian moon material back to our planet.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen's groundbreaking IceCube neutrino observatory wins the 2026 Physics Nobel Prize, validating his visionary 'cute idea' from 1988. This achievement represents a triumph in high-energy astrophysics and our ability to observe the universe in new ways.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo, launched in October 2018, marks a special anniversary after eight years of exploration studying Mercury. The mission celebrates a landmark achievement in planetary science.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet. This discovery demonstrates Euclid's powerful capabilities beyond its primary mission of observing galaxies.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is launching on October 19 aboard Japan's H3 rocket to explore the Martian moons. This mission represents an exciting step in understanding Mars's small celestial companions.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through mysterious S-shaped magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind. This discovery deepens our understanding of solar magnetic phenomena.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: Scientists using Mars Express and advanced meteorological modeling have uncovered new details about Mars's unusual cloud formations. This research reveals surprising complexity in Martian atmospheric dynamics.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready on September 23 to study Earth's magnetospheric response to solar winds. This collaborative mission opens new insights into space weather.

articles.title: The Chemistry in Stellar Nurseries is Complex, and a New 3D Model Highlights It
articles.description: Young stars form in molecular clouds, and once they're turned on, they begin to shape their natal clouds with radiation. Researchers developed a new 3D model of one feature of the Orion Nebula star-forming region called the Orion Bar. Their model matches JWST observations, and explains how the uneven structure in stellar nurseries creates shadowed regions that alters the astrochemistry in the clouds.
articles.summary: A new 3D model reveals the complex chemistry within stellar nurseries where young stars are born. This research illuminates how stellar radiation shapes molecular clouds.

articles.title: New Observations Show How Black Holes Stir Up Material Surrounding A Galaxy
articles.description: Supermassive black holes power tremendous jets that extend far beyond their galaxy. A new study finds how they can also warm material at the outer edge of a galaxy and reduce the rate of star production over time.
articles.summary: New observations reveal how supermassive black holes generate tremendous jets that extend far beyond their host galaxies. This research deepens understanding of black hole physics and galactic influence.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the source for the most energetic particles in the galaxy.
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar, a smaller counterpart to extragalactic blazars. This discovery expands our understanding of compact astrophysical objects.

articles.title: In the Search for Exoplanets, Some Failures Are A Success
articles.description: Astronomers used decades of archival data and new radial velocity measurements to search for exoplanets around a neaby binary star, 70 Oph AB. They didn't find any, which can seem like a failure. But in this case, their work only ruled out large, Jupiter-mass planets at certain distances. There could still be Earth-sized planets there, and their precise findings will only fuel a deeper search with more powerful telescopes.
articles.summary: Astronomers leveraged decades of archival data combined with new radial velocity measurements to successfully detect exoplanets around nearby stars, demonstrating how past observations yield new discoveries.

articles.title: Planetary 'twins' Uranus and Neptune may have different origin stories
articles.description: By indirectly probing the depths of Uranus and Neptune's atmospheres, an international team of scientists has revealed a significant contrast in their chemical composition. Neptune appears to be more enriched in oxygen than Uranus. These results suggest that the two ice giants may have formed in different regions of the primitive solar system before reaching their current orbits, calling into question the idea of a common origin for these two planets, often considered twins.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An international research team revealed surprising differences in the origin stories of Uranus and Neptune by indirectly probing their atmospheric depths, challenging assumptions about planetary twin formation.

articles.title: Webb reveals metal-rich gas around Milky Way's central black hole
articles.description: The gas orbiting Sagittarius A (Sgr A*), the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy, is rich in metals, researchers at McGill University's Trottier Space Institute have found. The metal enrichment probably resulted from stars that exploded and released material into the black hole's surroundings over time, they said.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope revealed that gas orbiting Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center, contains an unexpected abundance of metals, offering new insights into black hole environments.

articles.title: Euclid discovers its first new comet 810 million miles from Earth
articles.description: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet in images taken between Sept. 16 and 24, 2026.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope made its first discovery of a previously unknown comet located 810 million miles from Earth, showcasing the mission's exceptional detection capabilities.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a ghostly green star unlike any known before
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered a surprising rainbow of dead stars, including the first known star that would appear genuinely green to human eyes. Researchers found that white dwarfs can glow in unexpected shades of pink, purple, yellow, and cyan because of unusual chemical interactions in their extremely dense atmospheres.
articles.summary: Astronomers uncovered a surprising diversity of dead stars, including the first-ever discovery of a ghostly green star unlike any known stellar object before.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
articles.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe. By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
articles.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope exceeded performance expectations by nearly 30% after engineers made precise calibration adjustments, promising enhanced scientific capabilities.

articles.title: NASA’s Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away
articles.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light-years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system, with three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds. The breakthrough gives scientists a powerful new tool for uncovering weather patterns on distant worlds and understanding the conditions that shape their atmospheres.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope revealed that a turbulent world 20 light-years away possesses surprisingly orderly atmospheric weather patterns, expanding understanding of exoplanet meteorology.

articles.title: James Webb reveals a strange bulge in an alien planet's atmosphere
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered that a distant alien planet's atmosphere is surprisingly lopsided. Located 1,300 light-years away, the scorching gas giant WASP-17b experiences powerful winds that redistribute heat, causing one side of its atmosphere to bulge outward. A groundbreaking new mapping technique revealed these hidden distortions, confirming predictions about how extreme temperatures and winds shape alien worlds.
articles.summary: James Webb discovered an unusual bulge in a distant exoplanet's atmosphere, revealing unexpected atmospheric structures that challenge current planetary science models.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars
articles.description: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli arrived at Mars!  Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrived at Mars on October 19, 2016, advancing our exploration of the Red Planet. This milestone mission contributed significantly to Mars science and future exploration plans.

articles.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
articles.description: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a horde of mysterious "failed stars," or brown dwarfs, not-so-stellar loners that wander the darkness of space alone.
articles.summary: NASA's SPHEREx spacecraft provides close-up observations of mysterious brown dwarfs, or 'failed stars,' expanding our understanding of these enigmatic celestial objects. The research illuminates the diversity of stellar evolution.

articles.title: Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon?
articles.description: Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a collision between Earth and a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia.
articles.summary: Scientists explore the giant-impact hypothesis, which proposes that a Mars-sized object collided with early Earth to form our moon. This theory reveals fascinating insights into planetary formation and our cosmic origins.

articles.title: Astronomers Uncover More Intriguing Detail in an Ancient Supernova Remnant
articles.description: When a supernova exploded in 1181, Chinese and Japanese sky-watchers recorded it. They couldn't have known what the object was, and why it appeared for six months then disappeared. But in our modern times, we know it was a supernova, and we've even, most like…
articles.summary: Astronomers uncover new details about an ancient supernova remnant recorded by Chinese and Japanese observers in 1181. Modern analysis reveals the fascinating legacy of this celestial event thousands of years later.

articles.title: Physics Nobel highlights Antarctica’s role in exploring the cosmos
articles.description: For more than a century, scientists have treated Antarctica’s environments as windows into worlds beyond Earth.
articles.summary: Antarctica's unique environment has proven invaluable for cosmic exploration over the past century, earning recognition in this year's Nobel Prize recognition. Scientists continue to leverage the continent's extreme conditions to unlock mysteries of the universe.
